title: Why bridges have expansion joints

marks.ask: Why do bridges have gaps in them?

marks.label: Hot summer day
marks.ask: How much does a bridge grow in summer?

explain.say: Steel and concrete grow slightly longer when they warm up and shrink when they cool. Each metre of steel grows by about 12 thousandths of a millimetre for every degree.

explain.say: That sounds tiny, but it adds up over a big bridge. A 1-kilometre steel deck warming by 50 degrees, from a winter night to a summer afternoon, grows by about 60 centimetres.

explain.say: If the deck were locked solid at both ends, that growth would push with enormous force and buckle or crack it. So bridges have expansion joints: gaps covered by sliding plates or interlocking metal fingers.

explain.say: The deck also rests on bearings that let it slide or roll as it grows and shrinks. That is the bump and clunk you feel when you drive over the joint on a big bridge.

faq.q: Why do bridges have gaps in them?
faq.a: The gaps are expansion joints. Bridges grow longer in hot weather and shorter in cold, and the joints give them room to move without cracking or buckling.
asks: What are the metal teeth on a bridge?

faq.q: How much does a bridge grow in summer?
faq.a: Steel grows about 12 millionths of its length per degree. A 1-kilometre steel bridge warming by 50 degrees grows about 60 centimetres.
asks: How much does steel expand with heat?

faq.q: What would happen without expansion joints?
faq.a: The deck would push against its ends with huge force when hot and pull when cold, which can buckle steel, crack concrete or damage the supports.
asks: Why do roads and railways buckle in heat?

faq.a: Bearings are the supports between the deck and the piers. Many let the deck slide or roll a little, so it can expand and contract freely while still being held up.
asks: What does a bridge sit on?

faq.a: A finger joint is an expansion joint made of two interlocking combs of steel teeth. As the deck moves, the fingers slide in and out but always span the gap for tyres.

facts: Structural steel expands by about 12 millionths of its length for every degree Celsius it warms.
Concrete expands by a similar amount, about 10 to 12 millionths per degree, which is one reason steel and concrete work well together.

quiz.say: A 1,000-metre steel bridge warms by 50 degrees. Roughly how much longer does it get?
quiz.show: 1,000 m steel bridge, 50 degree rise: it grows about…
quiz.why: 1,000 metres times 0.000012 per degree times 50 degrees is 0.6 metres, or 60 centimetres.

wrong.2: That would make it 6 percent longer, far more than steel expands.
